newsitem.title: USA: FCC chairman to announce plans to step down.
newsitem.headline: FCC chairman to announce plans to step down.

text.p: Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt was set to announce later Tuesday his plans to leave the agency, sources close to the FCC said.

Hundt also was expected to ask President Bill Clinton to begin the process of finding a successor for the nation's top communications regulator. Hundt is not expected to leave the FCC immediately, the sources said, and instead is expected to stay on until a new chairman is in place.
Hundt has scheduled a news conference Tuesday for 2:30 p.m. EDT 1830 GMT.
The sources said Hundt was not expected to announce what he will do once he leaves the FCC. He was appointed chairman by Clinton and took over the job in November 1993.
Under Hundt, the FCC has had the huge task of implementing last year's sweeping overhaul of the nation's communications law.

Among those mentioned as possible successors to Hundt are Susan Ness, now a commissioner at the five-member FCC, and the agency's general counsel, William Kennard. Clinton nominated Kennard last Frday to fill one of two commissioner slots now vacant.
Another possible replacement is Kathy Wallman, now a White House economic aide and formerly the head of the FCC's common carrier bureau.
